The sentence now says income per person stayed below its 2018 level from 2019 to 2024, which the series confirms.

growth_story.headline: Hong Kong's income per person grew 4.7 percent a year from 2000 to 2007, then 1.4 percent through a run of shocks, reaching a new high only in 2025.
growth_story.arc: In the 1990s income per person grew 2.1 percent a year, and the Asian crisis brought the deepest recession in a generation, with a fall of 6.7 percent in 1998 and years of falling prices after it. From 2000 to 2007 growth sped up to 4.7 percent a year, as factories moved to the mainland and the city used its role as a financial center to become a service economy; after the SARS outbreak of 2003, growth ran between 5.6 and 7.9 percent each year from 2004 to 2007. Since 2008 the pace has been 1.4 percent a year: the global financial crisis hit a city that relies on trade and finance, and income per person fell 2.7 percent in 2009. A run of shocks from 2019 brought falls of 2.4 percent in 2019, 6.2 in 2020 and 2.8 in 2022, so the last decade averaged 1.0 percent a year against 2.8 in the decade before. Income per person passed its 2018 level only in 2025, when it grew 3.8 percent on strong technology-related exports.

threads.title: Asian crisis and falling prices
threads.text: The Asian crisis brought Hong Kong its deepest recession in a generation, and income per person fell 6.7 percent in 1998. Prices then fell for several years as the economy adjusted under its fixed link to the US dollar.

threads.title: From factories to finance
threads.text: Almost all of Hong Kong's manufacturing moved across the border to the Pearl River Delta, and the city became a service economy built on its role as a global financial center. Closer ties with the mainland drove this shift and the fast growth of 2000 to 2007.

threads.title: Global financial crisis
threads.text: Because the city relies so much on trade and finance, the 2008 crisis hit it hard, and income per person fell 2.7 percent in 2009. Growth since 2008 has averaged 1.4 percent a year, well below the pace of the years before.

threads.title: Shocks since 2019
threads.text: Several shocks from 2019 on brought three years of recession, followed by a long adjustment in the property sector. The IMF says the recovery is still incomplete and private investment is weak; investment fell from 33.3 percent of GDP in 1997 to 16.1 in 2022.

since_last_year.text: Income per person grew 3.8 percent in 2025 and passed its 2018 level for the first time, helped by strong technology-related exports. In May 2026 the IMF saw a weaker outlook, as the war in the Middle East weakened demand abroad and tightened financial conditions.

growth_story.tension: The data show income per person at its highest level ever in 2025, while the IMF stresses that the recovery is incomplete and activity is still below its pre-pandemic trend. Both can be true: the new high came only after income per person stayed below its 2018 level from 2019 to 2024.
